In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a population of strongly evolving galaxies at moderate redshift (z ~ 1) is required to explain the observed counts and background levels in all the bands.
the existence of a population of strongly evolving galaxies at moderate redshift, as suggested by deep galaxy counts, is a plausible explanation, but not a compelling one.
a dominant population of strong starburst galaxies at moderate redshift does exist.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large number of faint blue objects at moderate redshifts are expected to be detected by deep radio and infrared surveys.
the existence of a dominant, strongly evolving, and optically obscured starburst population at z = 0.5 - 1.5 can account for most of the observed excess in the counts at the faint end.
starbursts are a major source of background radiation in the radio, mid- and far-infrared, and X-ray bands, with contributions that are comparable to, or larger than those from AGNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the starburst population is likely to be a significant contributor to the diffuse background radiation in all these bands, and that the radio, infrared and X-ray counts are likely to be dominated by starburst galaxies at faint magnitudes.

, if starburst galaxies are the dominant population of faint blue galaxies, then they are also likely the dominant source of the diffuse extragalactive background radiation in all three spectral bands.
